overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals that first-person hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme planetary physics consistently drive peak performance (800–1,050+ views, up to 3.7% like conversion). In contrast, generic psychology factoids and over-recycled biological trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') suffer severe viewer fatigue, routinely stalling below 100 views with near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) achieved the highest retention and engagement on the channel.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person POV hooks ('What if you dropped into...') paired with hyper-extreme astrophysical environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) outperform baseline facts by 5x-10x.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on hostile cosmic phenomena characterized by bizarre material states and deadly sensory conditions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 to 53 views, 0 likes) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently generated channel-low engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Retire static pop-psychology trivia unless framed as a high-stakes dramatic narrative or visceral mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' were re-uploaded up to 4 times, with diminishing returns down to 17–34 views.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness constraints; never re-upload identical hooks or elementary school facts.
